newsitem.title: CHILE: Codelco board gives go ahead to San Antonio mine.
newsitem.headline: Codelco board gives go ahead to San Antonio mine.

text.p: Chile's state copper company Codelco said its board has agreed to go ahead with development of the San Antonio copper deposit in northern Chile.
"The Codelco board approves the start of the process...to achieve the development and exploitation of the San Antonio project," said the statement.
The deposit in the Third Region has reserves of 229 million tonnes of copper oxides and 310 million tonnes of sulphides.
Codelco plans to involve the private sector in the development of the mine, the second the corporation will build from scratch, it said.
"This decision is made within Codelco's policy to increase the value of the company through the complementation of businesses with third parties," said the statement.
Possible partners include Chile's private pension funds who have been hankering to be allowed to be allowed to invest in San Antonio which lies near Codelco's Salvador division.
San Antonio includes reserves from the disused Potrerillos mine as well as mineral from five satellite copper and gold deposits.
